Many people know the Red King Adrithyr, not many know how he got the title, or the crown. Adrithyr is the second born son of Calix the First, or Calix the Elder. Second sons so rarely rise as high as Adrithyr, but in his younger days he was quite the overachiever. In his youth he was heralded as a great swordsman, a legendary warrior that fought the with fury of fire, quite literally.

While quelling a small rebellion by the old Lords of Oligoth, house Rex, Adrithyr was said to have a blade clad in fire, rare and powerful, but not completely unbelievable. The thing that cemented him as a great warrior was the crown, it was as if the licking tongues of flame formed a crown over his head as he slashed through men, a crown of fire, a red crown for a red king. Of course then he was the Red Prince, and not the price meant to inherit the crown. So how did this great warrior Prince clad in fire obtain his father's throne? Blood.

Calix and Adrithyr both fancied a lady, the most beautiful woman in the realm, Lyanna Mournraine. She was breathtaking, with hair like drops of silver and skin soft as a baby's bottom. Every man who saw her dreamed of her, but Calix the Younger didn't have to dream. Calix was handsome, a strong frame, good features, and a well known warrior. It helped being next in line to the throne, and he courted Lyanna for months, but she always seemed distant. 

Distance was not their issue, as Lyanna resided within the same royal palace as Calix, the problem was that Calix wasn't the only Prince in the castle. Adrithyr was slightly more handsome, a slightly better warrior, and had the legend of his abilities to boost his stature. The Red Prince and Lyanna had been meeting in secret for years, and Calix II discovered it too late. The two lovebirds stole away in the night, just before King Calix gave his heir the blessing to marry Lyanna.

Adrithyr loved her, and he wouldn't giver her up for anything but his life. Calix the Younger loved his brother, and did not want war, Adrithyr loves his brother, but he loved Lyanna war. So, two brothers who did not fight for hate, but for love, clashed. At the castle of Whitestone a battle ensued, Adrithyr was vastly outnumbered, many say it was 5 to 1 soldiers in favor of Calix, but Adrithyr was a monster, and his tactics were astounding. He used strategy to create a trap, luring Calix's army into the valley of Whitestone, and using the confined space to kill them in huge groups using a rain of arrows and hail of spears. 

As the armies fought Calix and Adrithyr led from the front lines, unlike the kings before them. As they fought they met one another at the center of a large clearing, the soldiers made a circle, as the two Princes met for single combat. Adrithyr agreed to fight his brother, knowing he could not lose. Calix agreed to fight his brother, wanting to spare the lives of his soldiers, and hoping to save his own skin.

They battled for a short time, but Adrithyr clearly outmatched his older brother. As Calix fell to his knees defeated, Adrithyr's blade at his neck, he begged his brother for mercy, saying there was still time to save Lyanna. Adrithyr asked what he meant, and Calix explained quickly, as the two charged towards Castle Whitestone together. 

Calix the Elder had decided, that his sons were fighting for one reason, Lyanna. Hoping to reunite the house of Realmcrest, he sent assassins to "remove" the source of his sons troubles. Adrithyr and Calix reached Lyanna too late, finding her in a pool of her own blood, stabbed in the womb by a dagger. 

Adrithyr embraced his brother, the two of them sharing the grief over their lost love, and made a pact. They would march on Terraven, and take revenge upon their father. The armies stood with them, believing in the righteousness of their cause, as Lyanna was beloved through Estor as charitable and kind to the lowborn and the soldiers.

The battle was short, as most soldiers defending the King defected or surrendered. Adrithyr met his father in the throne room, and cut off his head before his father could utter a word beyond "Son-". The crown fell with his head, covered in blood spurting from the decapitated king, and Adrithyr took it up and placed it on his head. He sat in the throne as the blood flowed from the crown down the new King's face, the Red King.
